core_obligations: Set up the comparison: for an object of the category, base change both algebras and modules; the two modules remain isomorphic after the base change, the finiteness of the local extension gives both that the maximal ideal upstairs is the radical of the extended maximal ideal and that the base changed extension is finite (proof lines 6076-6083).

Relate the two vanishing loci: the first consequence implies that the closed set of primes where the two extended maximal ideals generate the unit ideal upstairs is exactly the preimage of the corresponding closed set downstairs (proof lines 6084-6090).

Conclude the equality of functors: for a prime in the locus downstairs, the localised module is flat over the base exactly when the corresponding localised extension module is, because they are isomorphic over the base, and this in turn is equivalent to flatness at every maximal ideal of that localisation; by finiteness the maximal ideals correspond to the primes over the given prime, all of which lie in the locus computed above, so the two functors agree (proof lines 6091-6104).
proof_roadmap: Base change and record the two consequences of finiteness (proof lines 6076-6083).
Identify the preimage of the vanishing locus (proof lines 6084-6090).
Reduce flatness to maximal ideals and compare using the correspondence of maximal ideals (proof lines 6091-6104).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the functor of points where a module is flat at a point is unchanged when the local algebra is replaced by a finite local extension carrying an isomorphic module (statement lines 6067-6074, tag 05P4). The proof works after an arbitrary base change: it records that finiteness survives the base change and that the maximal ideal upstairs is the radical of the extended one, uses the latter to identify the closed set of relevant primes upstairs with the preimage of the one downstairs, and then reduces flatness of the localised module to flatness at the maximal ideals of the localisation, which finiteness matches with the primes over the original prime. The comparison of the two vanishing loci is the substance, so the claim is H2.
